title: The Digital Infrastructure Universe Continues to Expand. Here's How to Benefit.
gist: BCG argues digital infrastructure has stopped being one asset class: 2025 global digital infra M&A value rose over 60% and US data center deal value tripled to $63 billion, but execution-heavy assets like B2C fiber face wider valuation gaps and holding periods stretched to 7.6 years. The actionable edge is asset-level underwriting plus seven 'misclassified seams' (MDU/bulk fiber, specialized data center services, stranded network assets, indoor wireless, embedded utility communications, physical-AI/robotics layers, and neofiber for AI clusters), while spun-out NetCos delivered a -4% five-year TSR.

insights.claim: Global digital infrastructure M&A deal value rose more than 60% in 2025 versus 2024, and the rate of change in how these assets are owned, valued and allocated is still accelerating.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A >60% jump in deal value marks digital infra as an active repricing arena; expect advisory, EPC and asset-owner tape to stay heavy into 2026.
insights.quote: In 2025, the value of global digital infrastructure M&A deals increased by more than 60% over the previous year.
insights.locator: The rules governing the ownership, valuation

insights.claim: US data center transaction value more than tripled from roughly $20 billion in 2024 to over $63 billion in 2025, per S&P Global Market Intelligence, showing deal flow concentrating in data centers and hyperscale-adjacent platforms rather than spreading across the category.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Capital crowding into core data centers means entry multiples there are the most competitive; the alpha is likelier in the adjacent, less-bid layers.
insights.quote: data center transaction value grew more than threefold—from roughly $20 billion to over $63 billion—from 2024 to 2025

insights.claim: A TMT Finance survey found approximately 83% of respondents expect digital infrastructure M&A activity to increase, yet in Europe the share of investors citing valuation gaps as the primary barrier to closing deals jumped from 48% to 78% year-on-year and 63% of US respondents named high valuations as the top obstacle.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Intent to transact is near-universal while price disagreement is worsening—expect announced-versus-closed deal slippage and more structured/JV deals instead of clean exits.
insights.quote: approximately 83% of respondents expect M&A activity in digital infrastructure to increase

insights.claim: The average infrastructure asset holding period stretched to 7.6 years in 2025 from 6.1 years in 2021 across the top 50 infrastructure general partners, evidence that exits for execution-heavy assets are measurably slower.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Longer holds compress IRRs and delay LP distributions; expect continuation vehicles, NAV financing and secondaries demand in infra funds.
insights.quote: The average infrastructure asset holding period stretched to 7.6 years in 2025, up from 6.1 years in 2021
insights.locator: Meanwhile, many execution-heavy and transitional assets

insights.claim: Assets historically bundled under one infrastructure label now behave very differently: cell towers still support long-duration, infrastructure-style underwriting, while fiber-to-the-home, newer satellite constellations and telecom central offices converted into data centers depend on operational execution, customer mix, utilization and reinvestment.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Underwrite at the asset level, not the label—applying tower-style cap rates to execution-heavy fiber or satellite assets systematically overpays.
insights.locator: The costs of misclassification have also become more visible.

insights.claim: Execution-heavy and transitional assets such as B2C fiber and cable face wider valuation gaps, longer exit timelines and a narrower buyer universe as investors reassess churn, terminal penetration targets, capital intensity and operating complexity, while capital stays abundant for scaled core data centers.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Owners of consumer fiber/cable stakes face a structurally thinner bid; discount marks accordingly and watch for forced-seller entry points.
insights.locator: The gap shows up most clearly in transaction outcomes.

insights.claim: The right diligence signals for separating durable yield assets from execution-heavy growth businesses are tangible operating indicators—churn rates, renewal behavior, repricing frequency and capital intensity—tested under stress rather than in good times.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A concrete four-variable screen investors can apply to any digital infra target before assigning an infrastructure multiple.
insights.locator: Investors must increasingly rely on tangible indicators

themes.theme: Returns Come From Operations, Not Rerating

insights.claim: Across global infrastructure deals from 2020 to 2025, 79% of enterprise value growth came from revenue growth rather than margin or multiple expansion, meaning the best returns went to owners who improved the underlying operating business instead of relying on valuation rerating.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Underwriting cases built on exit-multiple expansion are historically unsupported here; favor sponsors with operating capability over financial engineers.
insights.quote: 79% of enterprise value growth came from revenue growth, ahead of margin or multiple expansion
insights.locator: As measured by global infrastructure deals from 2020 to 2025

insights.claim: Broad exposure to digital assets now raises the probability of riskier outcomes because value creation depends on a wider range of asset-level portfolio choices, so diversification within the category no longer reduces risk the way it once did.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Index-style or broad-basket exposure to digital infra is a weaker strategy than concentrated, asset-specific selection.
insights.locator: In this environment, broad exposure to digital assets

insights.claim: Multidwelling-unit and bulk fiber plus embedded building access networks are valued on building-access control, portfolio-wide exclusivity and long-term bulk contracts rather than retail subscriber growth, and they show lower churn than open-access FTTH while remaining underaggregated because of operational complexity.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: An aggregation roll-up with better commercial execution is the identified value path in a segment with tower-like churn but no tower-like multiple.
insights.quote: These assets often exhibit lower churn than open-access FTTH networks, but they remain underaggregated due to operational complexity.

insights.claim: Rather than owning increasingly crowded and capital-intensive data centers, investors can capture AI-driven growth without concentrated risk by owning the capabilities behind build and maintenance cycles—construction services, networking, commissioning, cooling, power integration and life-cycle operations—including emerging supply chains for orbital data centers in space.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A picks-and-shovels route into AI capex with lower asset concentration; scarce specialist labor means talent acquisition and M&A are the scaling levers.
insights.quote: This opportunity also applies to emerging supply chains and capabilities in support of orbital data centers in space.

insights.claim: Copper networks, subscale hybrid fiber coaxial plant, satellite ground infrastructure and legacy central offices are discounted mainly because they sit awkwardly inside growth-oriented portfolios, and that structural mismatch—not poor economics—makes them attractive to buyers with a different time horizon, cost structure or shared-utilization thesis.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A classic forced-seller arbitrage: harvest, decommissioning, migration or shared-infrastructure repurposing of assets priced for the wrong owner.
insights.quote: Investors often discount these assets because they sit awkwardly within portfolios built for growth

insights.claim: Communications software and workflows deeply embedded in utilities, logistics and telecom operations are single-threaded around one communications stack, giving them strong contractual behavior, high switching costs and regulatory or mission-critical status—infrastructure-like durability inside what looks like a software business.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Software assets with genuine infrastructure duration may be underwritten at software multiples—an arbitrage for investors willing to reclassify.
insights.quote: single-threaded—built around a single, deeply embedded communications stack—with strong contractual behavior and high switching costs

insights.claim: As AI begins acting in the physical world, a shared operating layer is forming across robotics and industrial automation—edge inference, sensors, robot operating systems and fleet management—that, when shared across warehouse automation and industrial IoT use cases, could deliver the platform economics and utilization profile infrastructure investors seek.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: An early call that physical-AI middleware becomes an infrastructure asset class; watch for the first infra-fund deals in robot fleet/OS layers.
insights.quote: these layers could deliver the platform economics and utilization characteristics that attract infrastructure investors

insights.claim: 'Neofiber'—high-capacity, physically diverse fiber built to connect AI and hyperscale data centers sited in new power- and land-available markets—addresses a growing mismatch between where compute can be built and where network capacity, route diversity and rights of way already exist, with returns coming from aggregating scarce rights of way and regional corridors via anchor-backed platforms.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Power-driven data center siting creates a fiber build cycle in non-traditional corridors; scarce rights of way are the chokepoint asset to own early.
insights.quote: It addresses the growing mismatch between where computing power infrastructure can be built and where sufficient network capacity, route diversity, and rights of way already exist.
insights.locator: Fiber for AI Clusters and Computing Power (Neofiber).

insights.claim: Asset-heavy NetCos spun out from operating businesses delivered a five-year total shareholder return of -4%, the weakest of any telco archetype, and 5G and fiber-to-the-home rollouts have yet to meaningfully lift average revenue per user despite substantial capital outlay.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Hard evidence against the NetCo/ServCo separation trade that many telcos and their investors still pitch as a value unlock.
insights.quote: asset-heavy NetCos spun out from operating businesses delivered a five-year total shareholder return of –4%, the weakest of any telco archetype
insights.locator: For operators, boundary blur is no longer

insights.claim: Telcos hold latent AI-adjacent assets beyond physical plant—distributed facilities, dense fiber, enterprise relationships, trusted billing platforms, central offices, conduits and power-adjacent sites—that can be offered as a service or spun into separate offerings to capture data center and high-capacity network demand.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Screen incumbent telcos for repurposable real estate and power-adjacent sites; that optionality is rarely in consensus estimates.
insights.locator: Many operators manage portfolios that contain not just physical assets

insights.claim: Governments worldwide are pursuing domestically located and controlled AI training and computing capacity, frequently through joint ventures or minority investments with local operators able to satisfy security, data-residency and regulatory requirements.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Regulatory-qualified local operators gain a structural role in sovereign AI capacity deals—a source of non-market-priced growth for incumbents.
insights.quote: Governments around the world are seeking domestically located and controlled AI training and computing power capacity
insights.locator: Reposition ownership; don’t simply relabel assets.
